maria_support: FYI: customer reported a sharp increase in 502/504s after the 09:10 UTC canary. They also saw timeouts and billing spike for a small subset of keys. They attached request ids and a short repro.
jack_sre: looking at gateway logs now. I can see a clear jump in backend 502s starting 09:11, coincident with canary traffic. routing shows ~10% to canary variant `v2026-03-canary`.
tanisha_eng: which config changed in that canary? I deployed the canary; last PR touched auth-proxy cache knobs and batch windowing.
maria_support: customer sample: request id `req-7f3b2a` 
customer_ops: """curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'""" returns 502 with body "upstream reset by peer". They also reported some 401s earlier.
jack_sre: paste of gateway snippet: ```[09:11:22] gateway: upstream reset (peer closed connection) route=generate-canary target=auth-proxy-2 host=10.3.22.18```
oncall_bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert PD#847 triggered: 5xx-rate > 1.5% sustained on /v1/generate (hosted-inference)
sre_lead: initiating canary rollback now. Priority: reduce customer impact. Jack/Tanisha coordinate rollback + quick mitigation.
tanisha_eng: pre-rollback quick check: canary changed `auth_cache_ttl` from 60s -> 0s (intentionally for testing) and enabled `batch_window_ms=8`. I thought 0 was handled but apparently it disables sticky auth cache in auth-proxy.
jack_sre: that explains KV cache thrash. auth-proxy instances lost cache affinity and started hitting HSM/KMS more frequently; we see elevated latencies and connection churn leading to 502s.
sre_lead: rollback kicked at 09:22. Traffic reverted to stable config. Monitoring: 5xx started falling by 09:27.
oncall_bot: deployer-bot: rollback job completed (rollback-id: rb-3691234567) by deployer-bot at 09:25
maria_support: notified customer about rollback at 09:26; they confirm lower error rates on their side.
customer_ops: thanks. They asked for root cause and a repro so they can validate.
jack_sre: repro steps for internal QA: 1) deploy variant with `auth_cache_ttl=0` 2) send steady 200 rps with varied tokens 3) watch auth-proxy error: `authcache miss -> KMS 429/timeout -> upstream reset` 4) observe gateway 502s increase. I scripted a tiny repro: ```for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN_$((i%50))" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate >/dev/null & done```
tanisha_eng: fix proposal: revert `auth_cache_ttl` in canary config, add validation in rollout pipeline to forbid `auth_cache_ttl=0` unless an explicit opt-in flag is set, and add a safety throttle for KMS requests in auth-proxy. I'll open PRs.
sre_lead: also add a telemetry guard to stop canaries if 5xx > 0.5% for 5m. Current canary gating accidentally ignored the gateway 5xx metric due to a tag mismatch.
maria_support: next steps for customer follow-up: (1) send summary of actions and expected timeline, (2) offer credit for the 40m window, (3) share repro+fix once merged.
jack_sre: creating incident ticket INC-2026-048 with logs, timeline, and targeted postmortem owners.
oncall_bot: note: escalation channel pinged: @oncall, @sre_lead, @platform_manager
tanisha_eng: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra-config/pull/987 - includes guard and rollback of canary flag.
sre_lead: confirm: rollback + config revert live in prod, monitoring shows stable 5xx < 0.1% for 20m. Closing immediate incident but keeping incident board open for RCA.
maria_support: customer confirmed successful regen of requests and appreciated the quick response. Marking support escalation as resolved from frontline. :thumbsup:
